newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Major reassures Falklands of Britain's commitment.
newsitem.headline: Major reassures Falklands of Britain's commitment.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major reassured Falkland Islanders on Sunday that Britain's pursuit of improved ties with Argentina would not weaken its commitment to the disputed South Atlantic islands.

In a Christmas message to the 2,100 islanders broadcast by the BBC World Service, Major said he wanted "a stable and a productive relationship" with Argentina, which lost a brief but bloody war with Britain over the Falklands in 1982.
But he said it would not be at the expense of Britain's unchanging commitment to the remote islands.
"You have the right to live under the flag of your choice, and we shall continue to ensure that you enjoy that right, and that you enjoy security," the prime minister said.

"The Falkland Islands may be far from Britain, but you are, and will remain, very close to us," added Major, whose broadcast continued a tradition started by his predecessor, Margaret Thatcher, after the war 14 years ago.
Britain's commitment to the Falklands will be further underscored when Defence Secretary Michael Portillo visits the islands on January 2.
With rumours rife that Britain is planning a considerable cut in troop levels on the islands, Major said: "I hope you will let him (Portillo) know of your concerns."

Major said progress on joint oil exploration where Falklands and Argentine waters overlap vividly showed that it was also in the islands' interests that London and Buenos Aires should enjoy good relations.
The prime minister said one of the priorities for 1997 should be to make progress on an agreement with Argentina to manage fish stocks around the islands.
